hunt.justification: Social engineering attacks like ClickFix bypass technical MFA controls by tricking the user into running local commands. This hunt identifies the execution of those commands on the endpoint, providing a critical lead before the stolen tokens are used to compromise cloud environments.

meta.analysis: A simple detection rule for PowerShell launched from Explorer is extremely noisy due to administrative activity. This hunt provides context by stack-counting command lines for rarity, inspecting full script blocks, and correlating with DNS lookups to phishing domains within a tight temporal window.

stages.name: Social Engineering Phishing
observables: Email subjects regarding holiday policy updates
Look-alike SharePoint domains
Short codes (Netflix-style) for device login

stages.name: ClickFix PowerShell Execution
observables: powershell.exe
Windows key + R (Run dialog) instructions
Clipboard manipulation via fake CAPTCHA 'prove you are not a robot'
PowerShell commands designed to export session cookies

stages.name: Session Hijacking via Token Theft
observables: Cookie Editor browser extension
Access to Outlook from unexpected IP addresses with existing session cookies
Successful sign-ins bypassing MFA using stolen tokens

stages.name: Attacker MFA Registration
observables: Registration of new MFA methods (phone numbers or authenticators) by a recently compromised account
Entra ID audit events for MFA device changes

stages.name: App Registration Secret Manipulation
observables: New secrets created for existing App Registrations
Secrets with long lifespans (e.g., 2 years)
Standard user accounts interacting with the Azure management portal/Entra app registrations

stages.name: Privilege Escalation via Over-Permissioned Apps
observables: Apps with 'RoleManagement.ReadWrite.Directory' permissions
n8n workflow automation tool usage
Assignment of Global Administrator role to a compromised user via an application principal

stages.name: Device Code Flow Hijacking
observables: Logins via microsoft.com/devicelogin
Device code flow used for browser-based session capture
Unusual UserAgents or client applications requesting device codes

scenario.summary: Attackers target Microsoft 365 environments using social engineering tactics like ClickFix and Device Code phishing to bypass MFA or capture session tokens. Once inside, they exploit over-permissioned applications and register new MFA methods to persist and escalate privileges to Global Administrator.

meta.rationale: The lead query is focused on standard user workstations where Explorer-to-PowerShell execution is most likely to be a result of social engineering rather than administrative work.
meta.hypothesis: An attacker has tricked a user into running a malicious PowerShell command via the Windows Run dialog by mimicking a CAPTCHA on a look-alike SharePoint site to exfiltrate session tokens.

scope_hosts.description: Filter results to these hostnames; leave empty to examine the whole estate.

phishing_domains.description: Look-alike SharePoint and Microsoft 365 domains you have seen, for example from your mail gateway. The source research names none; the step also flags SharePoint look-alikes on its own.

references.name: Huntress — Three Attacks, Zero Exploits in Microsoft 365

blind_spots.risk: Without registry telemetry the Run dialog entry cannot be read, leaving only the process parent and script content for analysis.

blind_spots.risk: If the command line is obfuscated and script block logging is disabled, the specific exfiltration logic remains invisible.
blind_spots.question: What was the intent of the executed PowerShell script?

hunt.name: Endpoint PowerShell Execution via Social Engineering
hunt.description: This hunt identifies ClickFix tradecraft where social engineering bypasses technical controls by convincing users to manually execute code. It identifies rare PowerShell commands launched directly from Windows Explorer (the parent of the Run dialog), retrieves the full script block content to inspect for obfuscation, and correlates these events with DNS lookups to phishing domains within a tight temporal window. An agent weighs the combined evidence of rarity, phishing navigation, and Run dialog history to identify successful session hijacking.

nodes.label: Rare PowerShell launched via Run dialog

config.content: SELECT process_cmd_line, device_hostname, user_name, pid, time FROM hb_process_activity WHERE LOWER(parent_process_name) LIKE '%\\explorer.exe' AND LOWER(process_name) LIKE '%\\powershell.exe' AND ('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || device_hostname || ',') > 0) AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') GROUP BY process_cmd_line HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT device_hostname) <= 3
config.description: Find rare instances of PowerShell starting from Windows Explorer, which is the parent process for commands launched via the Win+R Run dialog. This step performs prevalence counting to filter out common administrative noise.
config.expected_signal: Unique command lines launched from the Run dialog. Legitimate admin activity typically clusters across several hosts, whereas ClickFix payloads are often host-specific or rare.

primitive_config.label: Rare PowerShell launched via Run dialog
primitive_config.content: SELECT process_cmd_line, device_hostname, user_name, pid, time FROM hb_process_activity WHERE LOWER(parent_process_name) LIKE '%\\explorer.exe' AND LOWER(process_name) LIKE '%\\powershell.exe' AND ('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || device_hostname || ',') > 0) AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') GROUP BY process_cmd_line HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT device_hostname) <= 3
primitive_config.expected: Unique command lines launched from the Run dialog. Legitimate admin activity typically clusters across several hosts, whereas ClickFix payloads are often host-specific or rare.

config.content: SELECT device_hostname, script_content, script_path, time FROM hb_script_activity WHERE script_type = 'PowerShell' AND ('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || device_hostname || ',') > 0) AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days')
config.description: Retrieve full PowerShell script block text to identify obfuscation or session cookie extraction logic that may not be visible in truncated process command lines.
config.expected_signal: PowerShell script blocks containing session or cookie keywords, web client calls, or encoded payloads.

primitive_config.label: PowerShell script block content
primitive_config.content: SELECT device_hostname, script_content, script_path, time FROM hb_script_activity WHERE script_type = 'PowerShell' AND ('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || device_hostname || ',') > 0) AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days')
primitive_config.expected: PowerShell script blocks containing session or cookie keywords, web client calls, or encoded payloads.

config.content: SELECT device_hostname, query_hostname, time FROM hb_dns_activity WHERE (instr(',' || '{{phishing_domains}}' || ',', ',' || LOWER(query_hostname) || ',') > 0 OR (LOWER(query_hostname) LIKE '%sharepoint%' AND LOWER(query_hostname) NOT LIKE '%.sharepoint.com')) AND ('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || device_hostname || ',') > 0) AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days')
config.description: Find DNS lookups to look-alike domains. The results allow the agent to verify if these occurred within a 10-minute window prior to the PowerShell execution.
config.expected_signal: Any resolution of look-alike domains around the time of the lead execution.

primitive_config.label: DNS activity for phishing domains
primitive_config.content: SELECT device_hostname, query_hostname, time FROM hb_dns_activity WHERE (instr(',' || '{{phishing_domains}}' || ',', ',' || LOWER(query_hostname) || ',') > 0 OR (LOWER(query_hostname) LIKE '%sharepoint%' AND LOWER(query_hostname) NOT LIKE '%.sharepoint.com')) AND ('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || device_hostname || ',') > 0) AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days')
primitive_config.expected: Any resolution of look-alike domains around the time of the lead execution.

config.content: SELECT device_hostname, actor_user_name, reg_target, reg_value_data, time FROM hb_registry_activity WHERE LOWER(reg_target) LIKE '%\\explorer\\runmru%' AND (LOWER(reg_value_data) LIKE '%powershell%' OR LOWER(reg_value_data) LIKE '%pwsh%' OR LOWER(reg_value_data) LIKE '%mshta%' OR LOWER(reg_value_data) LIKE '%curl%' OR LOWER(reg_value_data) LIKE '%-enc%' OR LOWER(reg_value_data) LIKE '%iex%') AND ('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || device_hostname || ',') > 0) AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days')
config.description: Read what was pasted into the Windows Run dialog. Windows keeps each Run command in the user's RunMRU registry key, so a PowerShell, mshta or curl one-liner there is the ClickFix delivery itself, even after the process has exited.
config.expected_signal: Rows where a user's RunMRU entry holds a PowerShell, mshta, curl or encoded command. People rarely type these into Win+R, so each row is worth reading in full.

config.objective: Determine if the rare PowerShell activity on each host is a result of a ClickFix attack. Specifically, check if a DNS lookup to a phishing domain occurred within 10 minutes prior to the PowerShell execution on the same host, and if the script content contains session theft or obfuscated commands.
config.description: Evaluate the correlation between PowerShell execution, phishing navigation, and script content.
config.expected_signal: A high-confidence verdict on whether a host was compromised via social engineering.
config.success_criteria: A per-host verdict of malicious, suspicious, or benign with cited rows and temporal correlation notes.

config.question: the triage verdict is malicious for at least one host based on temporal matching of phishing navigation and rare script execution
config.condition: the triage verdict is malicious for at least one host based on temporal matching of phishing navigation and rare script execution
config.description: Direct the response based on the agent's findings.
Stop immediate token theft and potential lateral movement.
config.instructions: Isolate the host. Revoke all active Microsoft 365 sessions and Entra ID tokens for the affected user immediately.

config.description: Verify the findings and assess the extent of the impact.
config.instructions: Review the triage verdict. Examine the script content for exfiltration destinations. Check cloud audit logs (hb_cloud_api_activity) for logins using the stolen tokens from the time of the PowerShell execution.
Log the result. If new phishing domains were found, add them to the phishing_domains parameter for future runs.
